title: Kampili Kingdom
capsule: Kampili was a short-lived Hindu kingdom in the Tungabhadra-Malaprabha doab of the Deccan, established around 1280 by Singeya Nayaka III, a former Hoysala commander who carved out an independent domain as the Delhi Sultanate's power disrupted the region. His successor Kampilideva (c. 1300–1327) extended the kingdom and sheltered Muslim refugees from the Sultanate, provoking Delhi's wrath. In 1327 Muhammad bin Tughluq's armies invaded, Kampilideva fell in battle, and his decapitated and straw-stuffed head was sent to Delhi; the women of the court performed jauhar. Just nine years later, the former Kampili core became the nucleus of the Vijayanagara Empire, founded by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I — possibly former Kampili officers — which would dominate South India for two centuries.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The approximate core territory in the Deccan is known from inscriptional and chronicle evidence, but precise administrative boundaries are unattested.
